name: RÙADH
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $655 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's jeans, cashmere sweaters, jackets and tailoring, jeans around $560–$580 and sweaters $1,000–$2,300, sold through its own studio and site, department stores and independent boutiques.

quote.q: Shaped by childhood landscapes, subversive femininity, and quiet resilience, RÙADH explores the delicate boundaries between self, society, and planet.

opview: “Shaped by childhood landscapes, subversive femininity, and quiet resilience, RÙADH explores the delicate boundaries between self, society, and planet.” — RÙADH (house), About, ruadh.com

craft_evidence.owned: no — all making is with named partner factories
craft_evidence.makers: yes, on nearly every PDP: SAITEX (USA, denim and canvas), Texmade Têxteis (Portugal, jersey), So.Pam Logistica Moda (Cerratina, Italy, shirting, est. 1986), Artigiana (Italy, cashmere), Sacchetti (Ita
craft_evidence.mills: yes: Lanificio Luigi Ricceri (wool, since 1848), Canclini (shirting, since 1925), Cariaggi (cashmere and merino); leather via Range Revolution (USA)
craft_evidence.madein: ~100% (70 of 70 styles state country and factory)
craft_evidence.heritage: no dated founding read; B Corp certified
craft_evidence.process: partly — factory and mill described per product (laundry, water recycling, hardware origin), not step-by-step
craft_evidence.reasoning: Every product page names the factory that made it and where (SAITEX USA, Texmade Portugal, So.Pam Italy, a Hawick knitter), and most name the mill (Ricceri, Canclini, Cariaggi). That is the most verifiable making in the batch. It stops at 4 because the house owns none of it: the makers are partners, not the brand.
